As a CASE for the 5X, I'd give it 5 stars. It makes the 5X easier to hold and likely provides good protection. For my use, I got this product looking for a holster, more than a case. I've used holsters a lot in the past, so have some expectations. Like the best holster I've used before, this one slides the phone in, phone face toward hip. It has some sort of felt-like material to protect screen and reduce friction as you take it in and out of the holster. As a holster, I'd have to give this product 4 stars. The reason is that the soft rubber inner case, rubs against the holster. It is particularly noticeable when pulling the phone out. Then, the hole for the charging port at the bottom of the phone stretches as it rubs against the felt. It feels like only a matter of time before it breaks. And I believe that the soft rubber part of the case might be increasing friction as it's pulled out of the case, making it somewhat more difficult to get. Not a "quick draw" holster. The price was good, and the product well constructed, but I'd ask designers to reduce friction in the holster, and do something different around the 5X charging port.

text: Like many tempered glass screen covers, this precision cover has a hard smooth top and and adhesive type bottom. The key here is to follow the instructions and use the guides to make sure you drop the screen down squarely the first time; and the other key is that you make sure there is no dust at all, not even any micro dust on the screen. So it's important to be in dust-free environment if possible, and also to follow the instructions carefully for preparing the phone screen, and perhaps even having a can of dust-off on hand to spray off the screen just before you apply the protector. If you find micrro dust under the screen after application, you can carefully pull it up with a very sharp knife and attempt to remove the micro dust, but if you touch the bottom of the screen protector you will mar it permanently. With that said, this case looks great on the S6 edge and fits perfectly. My only real complaint is how scratch-prone it is. I noticed scratches immediately after installing this case, caused by the phone's aluminum edges rubbing against it. If you have a Black Sapphire S6 edge, these scratches are quite visible. ~ OPAQUE VERSION ~ There are numerous differences between this and the clear-backed case. First, the plastic in this version is a bit thicker and sturdier than the clear case. The lips around the edges are a bit more pronounced, wrapping around the phone a little more. There is also a padded surface on the interior, protecting the glass back of your S6 edge. All of this amounts to better protection against drops, while maintaining a very thin profile. It doesn't look as good as the clear-backed version, but withstands scratches better and doesn't show dust that may get in between the case and phone. I would recommend this version of the case over the clear cover. Note: Both versions of this case do a good job at protecting the camera-bulge and screen when placed on a flat surface.

While I know my kiddo is hard on her phone (that’s why we have the case on it amiright?!), I still expect the protective case to hold up better. The poor thing didn’t even make it a year! If you need a cheap case and aren’t hard on your phone this is a cheap option. Seriously though, if you’re not hard on your phone you must be a wizard and I’m impressed. This case will work for you. I only snorkel and use it at the river or pool. So I’m not sure how it works in deeper water. But I love it! As a heads up, The salt water did need to be regularly cleaned off the outside plastic/glass while using during the day because it left a white film. But that’s just what salt water does, so it’s not an issue with the product. Also the water droplets on the glass while using the camera above the water did make some photos foggy or have light detracted in weird ways. But underwater there’s none of those issues. Just something to be aware of.

label: Positive
text: I bought this case for my iPhone 8 Plus after previously using a Spigen Thin Fit Hybrid on my last phone. I have had good experiences with Spigen’s products in the past, so I knew the build quality would not be an issue. I was looking for a case that would protect against scratches and the occasional short drop, and one that would be compatible with the magnet mount in my car. After researching available Spigen cases and a few other companies offerings, I settled on the Neo Hybrid Herringbone case. I have to say, I think this is my favorite case I have ever owned. I love the look and it handles well in the hand, but also slides in and out of pockets with no issue. My only complaint is that it is not designed to work with Spigen’s QNMP magnet mount system. My old case actually had a recessed area on the inside to hide a metal plate, which provided a great way to mount the phone in my car. However, I was finally able to make this case work with my magnet mount. While the case is not designed to be compatible, I was able to stick a metal plate on the inside of the case, and it works great. No, I can’t use wireless charging due to the metal plate, but the ability to use the car mount is more important to me. I don’t mind cables, and they charge nuch faster, anyway. Bottom line - if you are searching for a great looking minimalistic case, this one is a great option.

label: Positive
text: I've wanted something like this for a while now. I tried to 3D print one but couldn't get all of the parts to fit exactly. This device offers several enhancements over that basic design plus is very easy to use at a reasonable price. This mount comes in two parts, with most of the weight in the ballhead which is all metal except the parts on the threaded screws. The part with the phone clamp is mostly plastic except the threaded inserts and internal parts on the adjustable pieces. I thought both knobs on the clamp part were a little more difficult to grip and wish they had been a bit larger for making adjustments. I first tried the vertical installation and noticed the screw from the ballhead had come all of the way through the base of the clamp part and was touching the bottom of my phone. It was very easy to loosen the clamp a couple of rotations and tighten from disc platform on the post of the ballhead (it had arrived in the lowest position). The clamp itself was quick to rotate between vertical or horizontal or to open and swap out for my spouse's phone. Any angle was achievable with the ballhead too. I did find myself making a number of small adjustments on the clamp due to not paying close attention and clamping down on the buttons on the side of my phone. This is where I wish that knob were a bit larger so the longer diameter from the adjustment screw needed less force. Since it's off to the side, there wouldn't be any impact view, but functionality would have been increased.
title: Solid tripod mount for mobile phones

The back screen key does nothing as do most of the function keys. When using the back key to delete previous characters, it only works if you hold it down and let it erase everything that you have typed. I suspect this is a product from a company in the growing trend of technology accessory companies that offer junk that does not work but they sell a few million and then disappear. Hipstreet will not exist this time next year. Unless Google releases their own product we will all be reduced to owning a giant Droid.

text: I needed a replacement stylus for my Motorola Moto G Stylus 5G (2021) phone. These work just fine with my phone. However I have a couple of minor issues. 1.) label: Positive
text: I have been using the PhoneDevil (matte finish) on my iPhone screen for almost a month now. Overall, I have been satisfied, but not fully impressed. The good: The Feel - I really like the texture of the protector. My finger glides across it with very little friction. The anti-glare works pretty well. The bad: My screen protector got a small scratch in the first week. This surprised me, as I don't remember scraping my phone on anything that would have done this, but it happened. The scratch isn't that noticable, but if you look for it you can see it. That is the only scratch that it has after a month, so it seems fairly durable. But yes, it apparently will scratch under the right conditions. The matte effect has a negative side effect of slightly blurring the screen. I have always been a big fan of matte finishes on TVs, computer monitors, etc. for reduced glare, so I got the matte finish for my iPhone. However, when you are holding the screen about a foot away from your face the blurring effect from the matte finish is much more noticeable. Not terrible, but noticeable. The application/installation went fairly smooth, except I have a couple very small, hardly noticeable bubbles around the home button and the hole for the ear speaker. I tried to rub them out, but they wouldn't go away. I finally decided that getting rid of them was more trouble than it was worth, and decided to leave it as is. In conclusion, the matte finish is very effective at stopping glare, but does have a slight blurring effect. The protector has a good feel, but is not indestructible (is anything?) And the application went fairly smooth, but wasn't perfect. Overall, I give it 4 stars.
title: Good, but not perfect

I was careful to locate both the outdoor and indoor antennas. I even made sure that the indoor antenna is as far away as the cables allow and that it is at right angles to the outdoor antenna. I wish the base unit had some way to really check the operating condition other than just a color-changing LED. text: I got this headset to use while driving and walking outdoors and while it does a decent job for the price, it's got enough flaws to take a couple stars off. First, the noise cancellation isn't very good. I have people complaining about the wind noise when I'm walking outdoors in a very light breeze, and complaints about engine noise if I'm calling from my car. For casual conversation it's fine, but I can't make any professional calls with it, which is a little frustrating. The sound quality is also rather poor. People's voices sound compressed and there's often noise distortion on the line. A lot of background noise from the other end that I never had problems with on my previous headset come through this one and often obscure what the other person is saying. Again, it's fine for casual conversation, but is still frustrating. Battery life has been very good, though. The speaker is very loud and easy to hear, which was eventually the problem on my last headset. And the price is much less than what I had paid for my last headset, which only lasted a year. For the issues with noise cancellation and audio compression I would honestly expect it to be cheaper, but at least for now it's getting the job done.

I literally never have to worry about that ever again. The device itself is cute. The metal feels nice. The controls are very fitted and feel like they're quality. I'm driving it with a 400W amp not cranked and getting some distortion a lot sooner than I expected. The stand is pretty sturdy & the telescoping arm is quite stable in just about any position. The lights have 3 different shades of white, varying from cool to warm, and 3 levels of brightness, controlled by buttons attached to the cord. There's a compartment on the bottom that looks like it's for batteries, but it's just for storing the cord & remote. I really hate the cord! It's not particularly long, and does not come with anything to plug into - it's just a USB connection & you have to supply your own power hub. Which would have been fine a few years ago, but now that every gadget is switching to USB-C, I actually could not find an old USB hub! I tried plugging it into the USB port in my desktop computer, but computer did NOT like that & shut it off immediately every time I tried to turn it on. Finally my husband was able to dig out an old USB wall hub to plug it into, but that greatly restricts where you can take photos because the cord isn't very long. Needs to either switch inputs to USB-C so it will work with current chargers & hubs, or include it's own wall hub.

I consider this case my city-ish, office, going out case. It's for looks, and accomplishes that well. I keep a regular Apple case handy for things like sports, outdoors, etc... whenever I feel the protection of a full, rubberized case is necessary. No problem. There may be some GPS interference when using the bumper case. I live comparison tested it with another iPhone (no case) - the phone with bumper had greater difficulty with general navigation. I tried it a second time (in a vehicle) and had no problem. Maybe it was the case, maybe it was something else. Just keep the screwdriver with you and if it becomes a problem, remove the bumper. The first is that the "clip" portion can rotate to vertical or horizontal so that in the vertical position it will clip to the vertical vent. This works fine. Unfortunately the second feature shown in the pictures was not included on the product I received. The second feature was that the stabilizer "feet" could adjust inward. See, on a horizontal vent the clip can adjust up and down so that the feet can rest on something sturdy because the vent itself will allow for the up/down adjustment. On most vertical vents, the vents slats only move left and right. Therefore the lower feet need to be able to adjust inward; otherwise, they are just left hanging out in the air with nothing to rest on. The picture showed that this product had that adjustment, but the product I received just had the static, non-adjustable feet like my old mount. If the product I received had been as pictured, it probably would have got 4 or 5 starts, but since it didn't have the ability to work on my vertical vents I had to send it back.

text: I have gone through a few of these charging cables for my Fitbit Sense. With the purchase of these, I realized something that should have been obvious before. The reason these break is because the magnets pull the adapter onto the watch before you can get the pins in alignment with the indented charging points. This causes the weak little spring-loaded pins to retract sharply. After not too many times of this, the springs start to fail and the pins retract into the housing of the charging cable, never to emerge again. The secret is to put an edge down first and then control how you ease the cable onto the back of the watch so you don't stress the pins. This cable has already lasted twice as long as the last one and I don't think it's because of the superior quality. Read the reviews -- they ALL have this problem because it is a Fitbit design problem, not a charging cable problem.

I used an inline charge meter to test these cables with a couple different Anker chargers I have. With the battery of my 4s under 50%, all five cables could only charge my device at 0.8 amps. When I used a three foot long Monoprice 28/24 AWG micro usb cable with a 30 pin adapter, the charge rate increased to 0.95 - 1.0 amps at 5.0 volts. My conclusion is that this cable is approximately 16-20% slower than a decent cable from Monoprice. I haven't done a teardown of this cable, which I'm tempted to do, but the conclusion that I draw from this test is that the power conductor wires in the cable are possibly undersized if you need a full charge rate of 1.0 amps. If time is not of the essence and you're happy charging at 0.8 amps then the cable is fine. I certainly wouldn't call this a "premium" product, as the title describes it. I had a hard time deciding between 2 or 3 stars. But for the claim that this was a premium cable I would have rated the product as three stars. There is a one star penalty for creating an expectation and not meeting it. That said, I've used these cables for overnight charging for three months and they still work. When the GPS was fully charged, I would plug the PowerCore into the usb ports on the cargo van and it would charge and be ready to recharge the GPS. My fault, I am becoming totally dependent on GPS. I could have used my cell phone, but I hate that tiny screen for GPS purposes. label: Positive
text: I bought this charger to replace a Ray-O-Vac battery charger that I had a number of years that caused my batteries to get very hot while charging them. I use this charger to charge AA NiMH batteries. I have not tried charging other size batteries. When you insert a battery into the charger it will tell you roughly how much capacity is left. Then, it will go through a refresh cycle, if needed. Then, the charging process begins. High-capacity batteries charge between 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours, which is quick compared to my older charger that used to run overnight. The batteries get a little warm, but not as hot as they did in my older charger. Each cell is charged and managed individually and not in pairs. This comes in handy since I have a couple of devices that use 3 batteries. Being able to charge up to 12 AA batteries at once is handy for us since we have battery-powered candles on our windows sills. There are LED indicators that tell you the status of each cell. The unit also charges AAA, C, D and 9-Volt cells. I have not charged these sizes, yet. I only wish the unit was a little cheaper. Other than the price, I think it works great. It charges our batteries quickly and we can charge 12 AA batteries simultaneously.
title: If you have lots of batteries to charge at once, this charger is for you!

(Or at least it was for us- likely due to the outdoor & indoor antenna being too close together on our part). Its difficult to position the inside antenna and outside antenna far enough apart (~20 feet) if you're in a small house/RV, and this makes a BIG difference. Overall great buy and would do it again. Even with our signal limitations, we positioned our wifi hotspot (verizon jetpack) right in front of the antenna so our internet speed was improved a great deal. Cons: The card slots are too wide, so after a few months they have gotten loose and the cards can fall out. A minor nitpick is that the buttons on the side all feel the same, so it takes feeling and counting to figure out which one is which. The back of the case has tons of extra material to make the back flat rather than follow the natural curve of the phone. Look at the pictures of the camera and logo openings and see how thick the material is; it gets thicker at the outside edges. This is beyond protection and into just poor design. It makes it harder to put the phone in a pocket or anywhere else. The thickness of the cards in the front is unavoidable, but all this thickness in the back is unnecessary. I'm looking for a better case, but in the meantime this one provides great protection and keeps me from carrying my phone and wallet separately. Not bad and it is quick to market, but there are some weaknesses that I wish they would fix and will keep me looking.

I need to turn this Bluetooth speakerphone off and back on for it to reestablish connection. Given that the power button is tiny and finicky, this is not something I am willing to do all the time, especially not when driving. So overall it is a good idea but questionable execution. text: Here are the main things that are wrong with this phone: no expandable SD card and no headphone slot. So I went from an S10e, a much older phone, to a Galaxy Flip and lost much storage capacity and entirely lost the headphone slot. The second problem, the lack of a 3.5mm headphone slot, is so they can upcharge you for some crappy Samsung wireless earbuds that die after 4 hours. Wired headphones never die. That was at about 10am. It is now EIGHT HOURS LATER and it has only climbed up 22%. In EIGHT HOURS. So I read the small details. It recommends a block with 5v/2a or 5v/2,4A power. I checked mine. It is 5v/.3 which is waay too weak for this (but works great with our phones). I checked another block here, it is 5v./1.55 I checked another. It is 5v/1a. So not one single block in our home is the recommended size for optimal charging. You would think the manufacture would INCLUDE a block specific to its needs. Guess what we have go buy now.

text: Coming from a broken LG G7 ThinQ (Qualcomm Snapdragon 845 processor), to the TCL 10L (Snapdragon 665), raw CPU performance is roughly half of the highest-end modern flagship CPUs. If you are a big mobile gamer, this phone may not fit your needs. But for my workload; checking emails, watching YouTube, listening to music, texting, using Snapchat and other social media apps, etc, I noticed NO difference in everyday use compared to my old G7 ThinQ. The 6GB of RAM is very nice, and I have never maxed it out. Pros: -Great price ($190 at time of purchase and review) -6GB of RAM is plenty for the average user -Large, bright screen. Resolution is essentially an ultra-wide 1080p. Nothing that will blow you away, but it gets the job done a lot better than I was expecting. -Android 11 operating system with little to no bloatware/preinstalled junk -Worked instantly with my carrier T-Mobile, just popped in the SIM and it worked! -Shipped very fast for me, ordered late at night, arrived at 8am the next day! -Headphone jack! -Front and rear facing cameras are decent for the price -USB C -Very fast and accurate fingerprint sensor Cons: -Snapdragon 665 processor will not satisfy enthusiasts who want the fastest of mobile processors. -No wireless charging -4G cell network compatibility, no 5G. -Volume buttons are right next to the power button; I often accidentally lock my phone when trying to adjust volume. TL;DR: Amazing value for money. Not high-end by any means, but an excellent mid-range smartphone for the average user.
title: Average phone, Amazing price

text: I bought this in spite of the poor reviews because, well - it was cheap - and I kind of like to tinker. When I got the watch I immediately upgraded the software on the watch itself, and downloaded the latest Android app to sync it with. Despite using the latest software (on the watch and phone, both) I was unable to keep it paired for more than a couple of hours. When the battery on the watch got to ~70% it cut out and would not sync again until fully charged. If the watch was moved out of range and back again it would not re-pair with the phone unless I went through the entire re-pairing process from scratch. If the phone went to sleep, the connection would be lost. Overall, except during the brief periods (typically 15 minutes long) when the connect worked, the watch was useless. When it worked (however briefly) it was very nice and showed a LOT of promise especially with some of the plugins that are available. After I gave up on the Sony software, I then tried an open-source project called OpenLiveView that is available on Google Play. This was, remarkably, able to maintain a Bluetooth connection, and if the connect was lost - for example if I went out of Bluetooth range, just pushing the button on the watch caused it to re-pair in seconds. Unfortunately, OpenLiveView is in the early stages of its development, so it does not allow you to use plugins YET. Overall, I am going to keep the watch because it is so cheap, and wait for OpenLiveView to mature. I give the watch a three (3), for trying, and because of its potential once OpenLiveView matures.

I received a welcome text from UK Three with my UK phone number, but only the data was working. I got on a chat with tech support and we figured out the phone was not fully activated yet. About 60 minutes later (I saw somewhere it can take up to 2 hours to fully activate your service) I received another series of welcome text messages about the activation. Once everything was fully activated it worked like a charm. We initially landed in Athens, inserted our UK Three cards. We had mostly 4G cell service from COSMOTE almost the whole time (no service on some of the insland ferry transfers in the Aegean Sea, but that was to be expected). When we bought the card, it said we would get 12GB data+3000 minutes+3000 texts for 30 days, however after installing the UK Three app, we were pleasantly surprised to see we were given 16GB data and unlimited calls and texts for 30 days. It's a decent enough stand overall, but far from ideal.

title: It's not "Premium Leather", just cheap vinyl.

label: Neutral
text: The case is sturdy and feels well built. It fits my iPhone 5S snugly. I like the little lever on the side that connects to the Silence button. I wish the actual silence button was a lever not a switch. There is one big flaw in this case. Since the case blocks the speaker port at the bottom of the phone in order to make it waterproof, the designer cut a hole in the back of the case that is covered with a waterproof mesh to allow the sound to come out. The fact that the case allows the sound out the back instead of the bottom where the actual speaker is causes the sound to bounce around in the case and vibrate it. I tried to ignore it at first but it got so annoying that I had to get rid of this case and switch back to my old case. Bottom line: The case is very well made from a durability point of view. The one flaw is in how it deals with the speaker and sound. I was unable to continue using the case because of the flaw. **Disclaimer: I received this item at a discount, in exchange for a fair and honest review.**
title: Sturdy case. Fits well. Speaker port on the case is annoying.

I tried a Sony-Ericksson and a Samsung phone first. The Sony-Ericksson would connect and pair, but immediately power down afterwards. I couldn't get the Samsung to even pair up. Both phones would connect to regular Motorola headsets with no problem, just not this speaker. Finally, I tried an LG Optimus smartphone, and that worked flawlessly. Moral of the story is that Motorola needs to be more specific on what works and doesn't work with their products. I did check somewhere on their website (can't find it now - may have been taken down) that had a compatability chart, but that said both the problem phones should work. It's not "works with any Bluetooth capable phone" as their ads suggests.
title: Good product

text: This is an attractive comfortable band, with 2 closure magnets that keep the watch snug against the wrist during normal daily wear. The magnets do not, however, keep the watch tight enough against the skin for the activity tracking during even moderate activity. Granted, I have a small wrist (the end of the strap wraps nearly all the way back to the watch when it’s adjusted to fit snugly) but it loosened enough to lose contact during water exercise. If you only need a nice looking inexpensive band for work or play, this is a good deal. If you need your watch to stay tight enough for the activity tracker or health features to work, this isn’t it—it was disheartening to see only 15 minutes of activity credit after a 45-minute pool session.
title: Loosens with active wearing

I've even had to use my other hand to "press" down my index finger to bend it a certain way so it can fit in the hole. So we will see how long I end up using this phone case.

I debated if I would install another protector (since you get three!) but decided to wait 24 hours like the instructions say. I waited and I’m glad I did. The bubbles are all completely gone. Overall this protector feels like the factory screen. I cannot tell it’s there at all. I’ve had it for about a week and no scratches at all even with keys in my pocket. The only ding is that the install frame is for a XS max which is a tiny bit smaller. You can still use it but it bends a bit.
title: Best protector I’ve ever had. Will always buy these from now on!

The seller took 10 days to ship it and it came in a padded USPS envelope rather than a hard envelope, and as a result, was cracked and secondly, they shipped only 1 vs 2 that I ordered. After contacting them and waiting for 3 days they finally responded and said they would correct it. Another 10 days later only 1 came in the mail packaged the same way. No replacement for the broken one. Called them about return and no response. It was not even worth my time to deal with it, so I threw them both in the garbage and got bodyglove ones for us.
title: Horrible Product, Horrible Shipping, Horrible Customer Service.

label: Negative
text: Was so disappointed after reading such great reviews! Great product if you're purely using it to keep water, dirt, sand, etc. away from your phone -- and I was also able to comfortably fit in my passport and some paper money with my iPhone 6 that has a case on it. However, I'm not sure if any product can solve for the problem of being unable to tap your screen while underwater. I was not able take any pictures since I couldn't click (you could hit your volume buttons to snap, but holding the phone like that gets awkward underwater) so had to keep it on video mode, which is a pain when you're traveling bc you don't want your battery to die. Additionally, I took it with me on an elephant jungle trek since the plan was to go down to the river. The plastic on the pouch attracted so much dirt in such a short time and couldn't be cleaned off for some reason, so the pouch was pretty much useless after that point. Finally, while I admit that one of the strings detached due to a child yanking on it, the other end came off very easily a few days later and completely unraveled -- had I been in the water, I would have lost my phone without knowing it, so make sure it is tied to you and not just hung around your neck!
title: Pretty disappointed

I used to have one with a belt clip, but it would sometimes pop off when sitting down. This case with two belt loops and a clip isn’t going to be coming off unexpectedly. I highly recommend these cases, particularly if you are looking for one that looks a little nicer. Very satisfied with this purchase.
title: High quality materials & finish

text: Ordered this for the H810 variant, and was disappointed when after aligning it perfectly, my charger blinked and ceased to work. Now my NFC doesn't work either, even when returning to the previous sticker. For those that say I haven't aligned it properly, I peeled the sticker off the back and used scotch tape to perfectly align the sticker on the contacts while applying decent pressure to the wireless charging contacts. Still, no dice. Will try the QuickCircle case next, hopefully this sticker hasn't somehow permanently damaged my NFC, though not sure how that would be possible. EDIT: Newisdom got in contact with me, and after some impeccable customer service, I learned that a possible source of my problem was that I initially removed the black metallic sticker that came on top of the product. This is a ferrite sticker which serves to increase the transmission power, and is not to be removed. I would recommend not removing this, as it is easily mistaken for packaging, but seems to be fairly critical. Otherwise, they refunded me fully, and I am extremely impressed with the speedy customer service I received.
title: Don't remove the black sticker on top!!!

It still works fine, but the weight of the phone is a little bit unbalanced when mounted.

This qi charger uses USB C, HOWEVER, the AC adapter needs to be a quick charge 3.0/4.0 AC adapter with at least 18W per port. Preferably 24w if you can find one. text: I'm a little on the fence with this one because of the misrepresentation of the product. This product is not to be used as a case all of the time; you should only use it when your phone needs to be charged. Once I fully charged both the case and phone, I left the phone inside the case over-night just to wake up and find the case battery dead, and the phone battery of course was about 90% full. This product is a charger for your phone, its not a extend battery. You charge the case and the case charges your phone battery. Now, lets say you charge both the phone and case together and leave the case on and use the phone throughout the day. The case continues to charge your phone until the case battery is dead. It doesn't charge the phone battery when it gets low; it charges the battery the moment the phone battery starts to lose its charge. meaning if your phone drops down to 95% the case starts to charge your phone and it will keep on doing it until the case battery is dead. Now, this product is good when your on the go and you don't have means of charging your phone via power outlet or usb. Charge up the case, but don't connect it to your phone. Place case separate until you need it later in the day. Once your phone goes dead, place case on the phone.

text: For anyone undecided on whether they're willing to spend the extra money on this model as opposed to some of the cheaper charging stations available on Amazon, do yourself a favor and go with this one. The connector is on a hinge that lets you easily pull your phone off without putting stress on the charging port, and while it's on there it also has a little backrest for more even weight distribution. But best of all the adjustable height USB-C connector is an amazing little touch allowing you to perfectly adjust it so your phone rests on its case instead of just putting all its weight on the charging port which can lead to wear and tear as is common on some of the cheaper Chinese models available. Speaking of which, while it is made in China, Encased is an American company based in New Jersey that clearly puts plenty of care into their engineering which really shows here. They also didn't skimp out on the internal cable, because this thing supports both USB Power Delivery which enables fast charging as well as data transfer which means I can use it as a really cool dock when controlling the phone from my computer with scrcpy. The included cable for connecting to a charging brick is fine, but I opted to go with a stronger nylon-braided one which I've gotten pretty spoiled by as of late. All in all a terrific product that I'm sure you won't regret buying and which I hope will last a long time.

text: I've replaced iPhone batteries before on an older model, so this wasn't my first time inside a phone. Unfortunately, things started to go wrong from the very first instruction. The various instructions and photographs are so microscopically tiny, with such minute markings, that even with reading glasses it was very difficult trying to correlate the instructions with the actual phone. You really need a magnifying glass or a microscope for this. At the very least, the manufacturer should have printed the instructions at a reasonable zoom level. Then the cheap spudger broke while trying to extract the battery. Finally, the instructions were useless at guiding how to put the delicate connectors back together. The first time I reassembled it, there were vertical lines across the screen that weren't there before. I had to disassemble the connectors and reassemble them, and nothing - the phone became completely inert. I tried four or five more times to get the connectors plugged back in. Nope, dead phone. This stuff is delicate work, and it deserves much instructions that are easier to read, more informative, consistent with the labeling on the tools, and the tools themselves need to be up to the job. The cost to repair is going to be worth more than the value of the phone, so now I have a crisis replacing the phone. Not cool.

text: Background: I've been installing screen protectors for years. As a result, this screen protector is a nightmare for the Nexus 6. The product seems well made, is well packaged, and comes with all the things you should need for a flawless install. The fact is, such an install on the Nexus 6 is impossible. The corners are rounded on the device, and a rigid piece of glass isn't going to properly adhere to concave surface. This leaves an air gap around nearly the entire perimeter of the device. Look to some of the photographs, and you'll clearly see the problem. The newer revisions of the Nexus 6 protector have tried to fix this by making the glass smaller and smaller (to avoid the rounded corners on the outside of the screen) but as a result, the air gaps now creep onto the actual display of the phone. This is a huge bummer to me because the feel of the glass is phenomenal. I would love to have such a screen protector, but it needs to be manufactured in the same shape as the display--not completely flat and rigid. If you are really particular about your screen protectors, and want it to be just perfect, move on. This isn't the screen protector for you.

This helps drop all of the dust floating around straight to the floor prior to installation. No one likes to install a screen protector and notice a spec or two of dust beneath it. This screen protector is unforgiving when it comes to a "post-installation readjustment, so try your hardest to do it right the first time around. 2. Take your time. I know you want to hurry and get your new toy protected, but you don't want to accidentally drop the phone or mess up the alignment of the protector during the installation. text: I received this new phone as a gift, and I've had it for a few months now. I'm so pleased. The screen is big and bright, it's powerful enough to let me play any game I like, and it's never failed to perform any function I desired. The battery life could be better, but it's nothing you couldn't solve by replacing the battery if it really gets to you, and it's more than enough to get you through the day unless you're a huge gamer with a long commute. It also has a built in power saver mode, which I've discovered isn't standard on many smartphones. The camera takes gorgeous photos and the touch screen is perfectly responsive. The little options button being on the bottom bar of buttons is an absolute blessing; it makes getting to the settings a snap. I previously had a problem with Home crashing if I tried to open Apps, but this issue was solved with the latest Android upgrade. I really couldn't be more pleased with this phone.

I am not sure if this setup is in series or parallel but it doesn't work well. Regardless, I am having trouble powering a modern phone which has higher amp draw due in part to a larger processor and panel. Take this review for what it is worth. I am looking elsewhere to find a solution that can at least maintain a 1 amp output. Preferably 1.5.

Overall I’m really happy with the design. Then I did some testing. I was naturally curious if the displayed voltage and amperage was correct. I tested this with my USB meter and found it to be accurate rounded to the nearest decimal point. I did find that the power bank supported “quick charging” at 5V and 2.1 amps. I also tested capacity. Unfortunately I found that the power bank consistently only outputs just under 7000 mAh. In my most recent test the power bank provided 6874 mAh of capacity. This is over 30% less than the advertised capacity of 10,000 mAh. Some loss is normal but 30% new out of the box is unacceptable therefore I can not recommend this power bank. It’s really a shame that the manufacturer chose to short the capacity as it’s an otherwise nicely designed power bank. Pros Nice Design Useful built in cables Useful built in display Supports “fast” charging up to 2.1 amps. Cons Under 7000 mAh capacity instead of stated 10,000 mAh

text: This viewer is very similar to the Habor 3D VR Virtual Reality Headset, which I also bought and reviewed. My review is almost identical for this one. Pros: - Comfortable to wear. Face padding is pretty cushy, and the head strap is decent. The face padding is not as nice as the Habor headset, but it's still a faux-leather (minus the nice holes for breathing). - Interpupillary distance (IPD) and focal length controls. It's possible to change the distance between the lenses (IPD) to match your personal IPD, which is handy since no one IPD is right for everyone. The focal length controls are useful to get the display looking as crisp as possible, and can help with vision issues too (such as myopia). Note that I found these controls more difficult to use than the Habor headset; your mileage may vary. Cons: - No way to touch screen once the device is in it. It limits you to gamepad or very basic passive experiences. This is similar to the Habor. - Once again, no Cardboard QR code included with the device. This sucks. I wish they would include _something_. - Identical to the Habor (I think the lenses and geometry is more or less identical): Lens field of view (FOV) is wide, but the entire configuration is not good. The lenses have a wide FOV, but the phone's display is too far from the lenses, so you end up feeling like you're watching a big TV in front of you instead of feeling immersed. Overall, similar to the Habor, I wouldn't recommend getting this for anything but watching videos in VR.
title: I wouldn't recommend getting this for anything but watching videos in VR.

text: I'm generally impressed with the value for money for the Nokia 2. However, I recently discovered that the Nokia 2 is not fully compatible with all T-mobile 4G LTE networks. According to Nokia Customer Service the Nokia 2 TA-1035 model operates on the following bands and frequencies: WCDMA: Band 1, 2, 5, 8; LTE: Band 1 (2100), 3 (1800), 5 (850), 7 (2600), 8 (900), 20 (800), 28 (700), 38 (2600), 40 (2300) This means that the TA-1035 DOES NOT work on LTE Bands: 2 (1900) & 12 (700). You need those bands to use T-Mobile's 4G LTE service in many places. So, this phone is not fully compatible with T-Mobile. Unfortunately, I have not yet found a reliable way to check which 4G LTE bands T-mobile uses for specific areas. So, if you plan on using T-mobile, and don't want your service dropping as you travel across the US, you had better not get this phone.
